questions.question: Glaciers are generally found in _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mountains.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Glaciers** are massive bodies of ice that form in areas where snow accumulates and compacts over time.
 
• They are generally found in high altitude areas, such as mountains, where the temperature is low enough to maintain the ice mass.
 
• **Glaciers in mountains are formed due to the accumulation of snow and ice from the surrounding slopes and the compression of the snow under its own weight.**
 
• **Glaciers are also found in the polar regions, but those are formed differently due to the low temperatures and constant snowfall.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Plateaus are elevated flatlands that are generally formed due to tectonic activity or volcanic eruptions.
 
 
• **They can have diverse geological features, such as canyons, valleys, and cliffs.**
 
 
 
• Plains are vast lowlands that are generally formed due to sedimentary deposits or erosion.
 
 
• **They can have diverse ecosystems, such as grasslands, forests, and wetlands.**
 
 
 
• Mountains are elevated landforms that are formed due to tectonic activity or volcanic eruptions.
 
 
• **They can have diverse landscapes, such as peaks, ridges, and valleys, and they are generally colder than the surrounding areas due to the altitude.**
 
• **Mountains are the most common location for glaciers to form.**

questions.question: National Rural Employment Guarantee Act assures how many days of employment every year to every rural household?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**100 days.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **NREGA was enacted in 2005 to provide employment opportunities to the rural population and reduce poverty.**
 
• The act guarantees **100 days of wage employment** to every rural household in a financial year.
 
• **The scheme provides employment opportunities in various activities like water conservation, agriculture, horticulture, and livestock rearing.**
 
• The wages are paid according to the minimum** **wage** **rates** **of the respective state.
 
• The scheme also provides for unemployment allowance in case employment is not provided within **15 days of application**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **P.V. Narasimha Rao**, the prime minister at the time, first proposed the **NREGA act in 1991**.
 
• It was eventually approved by the parliament and put into effect in** 625 Indian districts. **
 
• NREGA was expanded to include all of India's districts as of** April 1, 2008,** based on the results of this trial project.
 
• **"The largest and most ambitious social security and public works program in the world" was how the administration described the act.**

questions.question: Fundamental Duties of the Indian Constitution are adopted from which country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**USSR (Now Russia).**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Fundamental Duties of the Indian Constitution were added in 1976 through the 42nd Amendment Act.**
 
• These duties were inspired by the Constitution of the former **USSR.**
 
• The **Soviet Constitution of 1977** had a chapter on Fundamental Rights and Duties of Citizens, which included duties such as respecting the Constitution and laws, defending the country, and working honestly for the good of society.
 
• **The Indian Constitution's Fundamental Duties were included to promote a sense of responsibility and patriotism among citizens, and to ensure that the rights of others are not violated.**
 
• **The United States of America has a Bill of Rights that includes fundamental rights, but not duties.**
 
• **Germany's Constitution has a list of fundamental rights, but not duties.**
 
• Britain **does not** have a written Constitution that includes fundamental duties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of fundamental duties is unique to the **Indian Constitution.**
 
• No other Constitution in the world has a similar list of duties for its citizens.
 
• **The Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee, which was formed in 1976 to study the question of amending the Constitution.**
 
• The Fundamental Duties were added to Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution, which is a non-justiciable part of the Constitution.
 
• This means that citizens cannot be punished for not fulfilling their duties, but they are expected to follow them voluntarily.
 
• **The Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution in order to balance the rights and duties of citizens.**
 
• The Indian Constitution already had a** list of Fundamental Rights**, but it was felt that citizens also had a duty towards the nation and society.

questions.question: Green Revolution increased the yield of food crops, and thus contributed _______ to the Indian Economy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**positive.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Green Revolution **was a period in India's agricultural history that saw the implementation of **modern farming techniques**, including the use of high-yielding **crop varieties, pesticides, and fertilizers.**
 
• The increased yield of food crops due to the Green Revolution had a **positive impact** on the Indian economy.
 
• **It helped in achieving food security, reducing food imports, and increasing exports.**
 
• The Green Revolution also led to an increase in **employment opportunities** in agriculture and allied sectors, leading to the overall development of rural areas.
 
• The use of modern farming techniques also helped in increasing the** income of farmers**, which further contributed to the growth of the Indian economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Green Revolution was mainly focused on wheat and rice production and was initiated in the 1960s by agricultural scientist M.S. Swaminathan.**
 
• **The high-yielding varieties of crops used in the Green Revolution required a lot of water and chemical fertilizers, which led to environmental concerns such as soil degradation and water pollution.**
 
• The Green Revolution was criticized for being focused on the production of a few crops and neglecting other crops, leading to a loss of biodiversity.
 
• The Green Revolution also led to the concentration of land ownership in the hands of a few wealthy farmers, leading to social inequality.

questions.question: Yeast and hydrogen peroxide create ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**oxygen.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Yeast is a microorganism that is used in many food and beverage industries for fermentation purposes.**
 
• **Hydrogen peroxide is a chemical compound that is commonly used as a disinfectant and bleaching agent.**
 
• **When yeast is mixed with hydrogen peroxide, a reaction takes place that produces oxygen gas.**
 
• This is because hydrogen peroxide breaks down into water and oxygen when it comes into contact with the **enzyme catalase** in yeast.
 
• The reaction between yeast and hydrogen peroxide is an example of an **enzymatic reaction**, where enzymes are used to speed up the rate of a chemical reaction.
 
• Oxygen is an important gas for many living organisms, including humans, as it is needed for respiration to occur.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carbon monoxide is a poisonous gas that is produced by incomplete combustion of fuels.**
 
• **Carbon dioxide is produced during the process of cellular respiration in organisms.**
 
 
• It is stable, inert, and non-toxic under normal temperature and pressure settings.
 
• **It also doesn't burn.**
 
 
 
• **Carbon** is a common element found in many organic molecules.
 
 
• At room temperature, carbon, which is categorized as a nonmetal, is a solid.

questions.question: ________ are located on the 17th group on the periodic table.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Halogens.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **17th group** on the periodic table is also known as **Group 7A **or** Group 17.**
 
• The elements in this group are known as **Halogens**, which include **Fluorine, Chlorine, Bromine, Iodine, and Astatine.**
 
• **Halogens are highly reactive nonmetals and are known for their ability to form salts with metals.**
 
• **They have seven valence electrons in their outermost shell, making them highly reactive.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Noble gases** are located on the **18th group** on the periodic table.

 
 
• **They are known for their inertness and have a full valence shell, making them stable.**
 
 
 
• **Chalcogens** are located on the **16th group** on the periodic table.
 
 
• **They include elements like Oxygen, Sulfur, and Selenium.**
 
• **They are known for their ability to form compounds with metals and nonmetals.**
 
 
 
• **Boron** is located on the **13th group** on the periodic table.
 
 
• **It is a metalloid and is known for its ability to form covalent compounds.**

questions.question: Which crops benefited more from the green revolution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Food grains.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **The green revolution was a period of agricultural innovation that took place in the 1960s and 1970s.**
 
• Its aim was to increase the productivity of crops and ensure** food security** for the growing population.
 
• **Food grains** were the main beneficiaries of the green revolution.
 
• Crops like **wheat and rice **were developed to be high-yielding and disease-resistant, resulting in a significant increase in production.
 
• This led to a reduction in food shortages and a **decrease in prices.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vegetables, oilseeds, and pulses** also benefited from the green revolution, but to a lesser extent. 
 
• **Oilseeds refer to crops like soybean, cottonseed, and sunflower that are grown for their oil content.**
 
 
• The green revolution led to the development of high-yielding varieties of these crops, which helped to meet the growing demand for cooking oil.
 
 
 
• **Pulses are a group of crops that includes lentils, chickpeas, and beans.**
 
 
• These crops are a good source of **protein**, but their productivity was low before the green revolution.
 
• New varieties of pulses were developed that were more productive and had better resistance to pests and diseases.
